newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS -BTP vol dips, Bunds tick up in dull trade.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS -BTP vol dips, Bunds tick up in dull trade.

text.p: Implied volatility of BTP options on LIFFE took a tumble on Friday, hit by a combination of time decay and the dormant trade resulting from a holiday in much of continental Europe.

"The Italians are all on the beach, and I've seen (Sept) vol as low as 6.0 percent," said a trader at a French house, speaking from a tranquil LIFFE floor. "It's looking a bit cheap there, a bit of a buy."
September BTP futures were down 0.36 at 135.10 by 1140 GMT. September volatility started the day around 6.7 percent, down from around 7.5 percent on Thursday.
Although the September contract goes off the board on August 20, December has yet to take over more than the leanest of volumes from the front month.
Meanwhile Bund volatility edged its way higher ahead of the U.S. open, postponing its expected decline until later in the afternoon session.
"The market tried to take Bund vol off, but didn't manage it," said a trader at a U.S. house. "We'll see more erosion later."
September Bund options were trading at around 5.47 percent, up from 5.30 percent at the open. December was at 5.1 percent.
September Bunds futures were 18 basis points lower on the day at 102.15.
